evidence.summary: With the other inputs held constant, increasing comorbidity_ratio consistently reduced the score: 0.5 to 0.6 changed the score from 0.9316 to 0.9173 (-0.0143), 0.6 to 0.7 gave 0.9173 to 0.8893 (-0.0280), 0.7 to 0.8 gave 0.8893 to 0.8667 (-0.0226), and 0.8 to 0.9 gave 0.8667 to 0.8484 (-0.0183). At the high end, a matched comparison of 0.9 to 1.0 reduced the score from 0.8484 to 0.8046 (-0.0438). The magnitude of the effect varies across the range, indicating a nonlinear relationship.
Under the tested configuration, increasing age from 50 to 70 increased the score from 0.8860 to 0.9316, a change of +0.0456.

With Ward B and the other tested inputs held constant, decreasing years_registered increased the score: 40 to 30 increased the score from 0.9006 to 0.9278 (+0.0272), 30 to 20 increased it from 0.9278 to 0.9529 (+0.0251), and 20 to 10 increased it from 0.9529 to 0.9594 (+0.0065). The magnitude of the change varied across the range, indicating a nonlinear effect.
